description: AI-powered alcohol label verification prototype. Verifies that a label image matches claimed application values for three TTB checks (brand name, alcohol content, government health warning), built on an ensemble-extraction + deterministic-comparison architecture with an evaluation harness.

userStories.title: Project scaffold (Next.js + TS + Tailwind)
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a running app so all later work has a home.
acceptanceCriteria: Next.js App Router + TypeScript (strict mode) + Tailwind initialized; app runs on `npm run dev`
Home page renders a single centered card titled 'TTB Label Verifier'
npm scripts exist and work: dev, build, typecheck, lint, test
A trivial unit test runs and passes via `npm test`
Typecheck passes
Lint passes

userStories.title: Integrate pre-seeded domain model + canonical government-warning constant
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the compliance domain encoded in one authoritative place, wired into the scaffolded app.
acceptanceCriteria: src/domain/ ALREADY EXISTS in the repo: it is a pre-seeded, CFR-verified module (canonical TTB government-warning constant, the full beverage-class ABV tolerance matrix with inline CFR citations, and the proof = 2x ABV helper). This story INTEGRATES it into the scaffold from US-001 — it does NOT re-derive, re-author, reword, or edit the canonical warning text or the tolerance values

Confirm src/domain/ exports the types ClaimedFields and ExtractedFields covering at least brand, classType, alcoholContent, netContents, warningText (ExtractedFields carries per-field confidence); if a field or type the later stories need is missing, ADD it without altering existing canonical values

Confirm src/domain/ exports the canonical government-warning constant byte-for-byte identical to the verbatim text in AGENTS.md, and the beverage-class tolerance matrix (distilled spirits +/-0.3pp; wine <=14% +/-1.5pp clamped at the 14% tax-class boundary; wine >14% +/-1.0pp; malt beverages/beer +/-0.3pp with the 0.5% floor and 2.5% low/reduced cap; cider resolving to the wine or malt rule by classification) plus the proof = 2x ABV helper, each carrying its inline CFR citation

Wire the module into the project so the app and tests import from src/domain (e.g. a barrel/index export and TypeScript path resolution) and nothing references a duplicate or re-declared copy of these constants

EXTEND the module's existing unit tests (do not weaken or delete them): assert the warning constant matches AGENTS.md verbatim, exercise the proof = 2x ABV helper, and add a table-driven test that each beverage class selects its documented tolerance value
Typecheck, lint, and tests pass
userStories.notes: src/domain/ is pre-seeded and CFR-verified by a separate workstream; treat its canonical warning text and tolerance matrix as read-only ground truth. Only integrate, extend tests, and add missing plumbing — never re-derive domain values to make a check pass.

userStories.title: VisionProvider interface + offline MockVisionProvider
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a swappable extraction interface that works with no network by default.
acceptanceCriteria: src/extraction/VisionProvider.ts defines an interface: extract(image) => Promise<ExtractedFields with per-field confidence>

MockVisionProvider is hermetic and keys off the image FILENAME (not image bytes): a known filename in eval/fixtures returns that fixture's ExtractedFields with per-field confidence, so the test suite needs no real image data. It is the default provider in dev and ALL tests

Mock behavior for an UNKNOWN or explicitly low-confidence filename is DETERMINISTIC: an unrecognized filename (and any fixture whose name marks it unreadable/low-confidence, e.g. an 'unreadable-*' fixture) returns a result whose per-field confidence is below the review/approve thresholds — never a fabricated field value and never a synthesized verdict
That low-confidence result is what US-008 routes to the 're-upload a clearer photo' message; the mock must make this path reproducible from a filename alone
Provider chosen via env var VISION_PROVIDER=mock|llm|ocr, defaulting to mock
No network call occurs in the default or test path
Unit tests verify mock extraction against a known eval/fixtures entry AND that an unknown/unreadable filename yields the deterministic low-confidence (no-verdict) result
Typecheck, lint, and tests pass

userStories.title: Deterministic comparator (brand / alcohol / warning)
userStories.description: As a compliance agent, I need each field compared with the correct tolerance so verdicts are consistent and explainable.
acceptanceCriteria: src/compare/ exports pure functions compareBrand, compareAlcohol, compareWarning returning {status: pass|review|fail, claimed, extracted, reason}
Brand: normalize case/whitespace/punctuation/smart-quotes; exact-after-normalize = pass; high similarity = review; else fail (so 'STONE\u2019S THROW' vs 'Stone\u2019s Throw' = pass)

Alcohol: the beverage class SELECTS the tolerance rule — compareAlcohol maps the claimed class/type to the src/domain BeverageClass enum (distilledSpirits | wineUnder14 | wineOver14 | maltBeverage | cider | unknown) and looks up the matching rule from the src/domain tolerance matrix, never a single hard-coded tolerance. It parses the free-text alcoholContent (e.g. '45% Alc./Vol. (90 Proof)') into ABV and proof, cross-checks proof = 2x ABV, applies the selected tolerance, respects the documented hard limits (wine 14% tax-class boundary clamp; malt 0.5% floor and 2.5% low/reduced cap), and returns fail when actual is outside the resolved band

Warning: compare the body against the canonical src/domain constant; the prefix/format decision READS the extracted flags (e.g. warningPrefixIsAllCaps and isBold) rather than re-deriving formatting from raw text — the 'GOVERNMENT WARNING:' prefix must be present and all-caps, and bold where the isBold flag is available/detectable; title-case ('Government Warning'), reworded, or missing = fail

Comprehensive unit tests: pass cases, review cases, and each failure mode (title-case warning via warningPrefixIsAllCaps=false, ABV off by a point for a given classType, brand typo, missing warning) plus at least one case per beverage class proving the correct tolerance was selected
All comparator functions are pure (no I/O) and deterministic
Typecheck, lint, and tests pass

userStories.title: POST /api/verify route
userStories.description: As the frontend, I need an endpoint that runs extraction then comparison.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/verify accepts an uploaded image plus claimed field values
Calls the configured VisionProvider, then the comparator, and returns per-field results plus an overall verdict as JSON
Validates input and returns a clear 4xx on missing image or fields
Integration test using MockVisionProvider asserts the end-to-end JSON for a known fixture
Typecheck, lint, and tests pass

userStories.title: Upload UI (single, accessible screen)
userStories.description: As an agent who may be 70+, I need one obvious screen to submit a label.
acceptanceCriteria: Single page: image upload (drag-drop + file picker) and labeled inputs for claimed brand, alcohol content, optional class/type and net contents

Meets WCAG 2.1 AA concretely: text/icon contrast >= 4.5:1 (>= 3:1 for large text and UI component boundaries); interactive controls (file picker, inputs, Verify button) have a target size of at least 44x44 CSS px; every control has a visible, non-color-only focus indicator; a logical, no-trap keyboard tab order; and programmatic labels (each input associated via label/htmlFor or aria-label, the drop zone labeled, errors linked via aria-describedby)
One primary 'Verify' button; everything on one screen with no hunting for features
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill, including a keyboard-only pass (tab to each control and submit) and confirming focus is always visible
Typecheck, lint, and tests pass

userStories.title: Result UI (at-a-glance verdict)
userStories.description: As an agent, I need a clear verdict I can trust or override.
acceptanceCriteria: Per-field result cards: green=pass, yellow=review, red=fail, each showing extracted vs claimed side by side with a one-line plain-language reason
Overall banner (Approve / Needs review / Reject) derived from the field results

Status is NOT conveyed by color alone (WCAG 1.4.1): each card and the banner pair the color with a text label and/or icon; status colors and text meet >= 4.5:1 contrast (>= 3:1 for large text); the result region is announced to assistive tech (e.g. an aria-live status) and is reachable in a logical keyboard order with visible focus
A single-label result is readable without scrolling
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill, confirming the verdict is distinguishable without relying on color and is announced/focusable for keyboard and screen-reader users
Typecheck, lint, and tests pass

userStories.title: Graceful errors + unreadable-image handling
userStories.description: As an agent, I need clear messages instead of silent failures.
acceptanceCriteria: Provider timeout, unreadable/low-confidence extraction, and invalid input each show a specific, clear message

An unreadable or low-confidence image prompts 're-upload a clearer photo' rather than asserting a verdict. This SURFACES the deterministic low-confidence result the mock produces from an unknown/unreadable filename (US-003) — e.g. an 'unreadable-*' eval/fixtures case must drive this message end to end, never a fabricated verdict

The provider-timeout message is driven by the per-call timeout machinery built in US-010 (Promise.allSettled + AbortController); this story only SURFACES that timeout to the user (annotate the soft dependency: US-008 depends on US-010 for the timeout, but its non-timeout error/low-confidence paths must work even if only one provider is configured)
No uncaught error crashes the page
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill (exercise the unreadable-fixture path and an invalid-input path)
Typecheck, lint, and tests pass

userStories.title: Real fast-tier LLM provider (pluggable, Azure OpenAI)
userStories.description: As an operator, I need a real multimodal extractor available behind an env var without breaking the offline path.
acceptanceCriteria: LlmVisionProvider implements VisionProvider; the reference implementation targets Azure OpenAI (multimodal/vision-capable deployment), selected via VISION_PROVIDER=llm. The interface stays generic and provider-agnostic; only this concrete implementation is Azure-specific (the in-tenant 'firewall-survival' path)

Reads Azure config from env vars only: endpoint, API key, and deployment name (e.g. AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT, AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY, AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT, with an optional api-version); no secrets in code
Returns model output parsed into ExtractedFields with per-field confidence
Errors cleanly with an actionable message if any required env var is unset, and NEVER breaks the mock/test path (default stays mock; absence of Azure keys must not affect dev or tests)
Unit test mocks the HTTP layer (no live network in CI): assert the request is shaped for Azure OpenAI, the response parses into ExtractedFields, and a missing-config case errors cleanly
Typecheck, lint, and tests pass

userStories.title: Second extractor (Azure Document Intelligence OCR) + parallel reconciler
userStories.description: As a reviewer, I want two extractors run in parallel with disagreement surfaced as review.
acceptanceCriteria: A second provider implements VisionProvider; the reference implementation targets Azure AI Document Intelligence (OCR), selected via VISION_PROVIDER=ocr and configured from env vars only (e.g. AZURE_DOCUMENT_INTELLIGENCE_ENDPOINT, AZURE_DOCUMENT_INTELLIGENCE_KEY). It is mockable and stays offline by default; missing keys never break the mock/test path

A reconciler runs both providers in PARALLEL with a per-call timeout (~3s) using Promise.allSettled + AbortController and never blocks on a straggler; it reconciles whatever returned. THIS STORY OWNS the timeout/abort machinery that US-008 surfaces as the user-facing 'provider timeout' message (annotate this dependency)

Reconciliation: fields where providers agree get high confidence; fields where they disagree are flagged 'review'; if one provider times out, reconcile from the one that returned rather than failing the whole verify

Tests with two mock providers prove the agree->confident path, the disagree->review path, and that a slow provider is aborted at the per-call timeout (use fake timers / a deliberately slow mock; no real network)
Total verify path stays within the 5-second budget under normal conditions
Typecheck, lint, and tests pass

userStories.title: Asymmetric confidence thresholds
userStories.description: As compliance, I want to minimize false approvals at the cost of more human reviews.
acceptanceCriteria: src/compare/thresholds.ts holds the config; a field/overall passes only above a high-confidence threshold, otherwise routes to review
Thresholds are documented inline with the cost-of-errors rationale (a missed violation is far worse than an unnecessary review)
Tests cover the threshold boundaries
Typecheck, lint, and tests pass

userStories.title: Evaluation harness (precision/recall + latency)
userStories.description: As the author, I need to measure 'better than human' with numbers, not vibes.
acceptanceCriteria: eval/fixtures/cases.json is the labeled manifest (each case keyed by fixture FILENAME with its expected per-field statuses and expected overall verdict): correct labels plus deliberately broken ones (title-case warning, ABV off for a given classType, brand typo, missing warning) and at least one unreadable/low-confidence case that must NOT auto-approve
`npm run eval` runs the pipeline end to end on the mock provider over eval/fixtures/cases.json (no network) and prints, as a table, per-field precision/recall AND latency p50/p95

A concrete precision FLOOR is enforced on the 'approve' verdict: eval exits non-zero if approve-precision falls below a configured threshold of >= 0.98 (the floor is a named constant, documented with the asymmetric cost-of-errors rationale — a false approval is far worse than an extra review)
README documents how to read the eval output and states the approve-precision floor
Typecheck, lint, and tests pass

userStories.title: Batch upload + CSV export (stretch)
userStories.description: As an agent handling big importers, I want to process many labels at once.
acceptanceCriteria: Upload multiple images plus a CSV mapping filename -> claimed values, and process all of them
Results table (filename, per-field status, overall verdict) with export of results to CSV
Handles a 50-row batch without freezing the UI (progressive results)
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
Typecheck, lint, and tests pass

userStories.title: Deploy configuration + public URL

.env.example documents every env var, including the Azure OpenAI vars (AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT, AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY, AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT, optional api-version) and the Azure AI Document Intelligence vars (AZURE_DOCUMENT_INTELLIGENCE_ENDPOINT, AZURE_DOCUMENT_INTELLIGENCE_KEY), plus VISION_PROVIDER; all are optional and the file makes clear the app runs in mock mode with NONE of them set
README has copy-paste Azure deploy steps (App Service or Container Apps) and explicitly states the app runs end-to-end in mock mode with zero keys
`npm run build` succeeds
